project.name: cargotracker-domain
project.description: Domain layer of the Eclipse Cargo Tracker Jakarta EE application: cargo, delivery, itinerary, handling and location models plus a specification pattern.

nodes.name: Cargo.java
nodes.summary: JPA entity for the Cargo aggregate root, holding tracking id, origin, route specification, itinerary and delivery progress.

nodes.name: Cargo
nodes.summary: Aggregate root representing a shipment; supports rerouting via specifyNewRoute/assignToRoute and recomputes Delivery from handling history.

nodes.name: specifyNewRoute
nodes.summary: Assigns a new route specification and recalculates delivery routing status.

nodes.name: assignToRoute
nodes.summary: Assigns an itinerary to the cargo and updates delivery on routing.

nodes.name: deriveDeliveryProgress
nodes.summary: Recomputes the delivery snapshot from a HandlingHistory.

nodes.name: equals
nodes.summary: Entity equality based on tracking id.

nodes.name: Delivery.java
nodes.summary: Embeddable value object summarizing cargo delivery status derived from the last handling event, route specification and itinerary.

nodes.name: Delivery
nodes.summary: Immutable delivery snapshot computing transport status, location, voyage, misdirection, ETA, next expected activity and routing status.

nodes.name: derivedFrom
nodes.summary: Factory deriving a Delivery from route specification, itinerary and handling history.

nodes.name: calculateTransportStatus
nodes.summary: Maps the last handling event type to a TransportStatus.

nodes.name: calculateNextExpectedActivity
nodes.summary: Determines the next expected handling activity based on last event and itinerary.

nodes.name: calculateRoutingStatus
nodes.summary: Computes routing status from itinerary and route specification.

nodes.name: TrackingId.java
nodes.summary: Value object wrapping the unique string identifier of a Cargo.

nodes.name: TrackingId
nodes.summary: Embeddable tracking identifier with value-based equality.

nodes.name: HandlingEvent.java
nodes.summary: JPA entity for handling events (load, unload, receive, claim, customs) registered against a cargo, voyage and location.

nodes.name: HandlingEvent
nodes.summary: Domain event entity with nested Type enum, validating voyage requirements per event type.

nodes.name: HandlingHistory.java
nodes.summary: Value object holding the ordered handling events of a cargo and exposing the most recent completed event.

nodes.name: HandlingHistory
nodes.summary: Wraps handling events; returns distinct events by completion time and latest completed event.

nodes.name: getMostRecentlyCompletedEvent
nodes.summary: Returns the latest completed handling event if any.

nodes.name: DomainObjectUtils.java
nodes.summary: Small shared utility providing null-safe helpers for domain objects.

nodes.name: DomainObjectUtils
nodes.summary: Static utility class offering nullSafe for iterables.

nodes.name: Itinerary.java
nodes.summary: Embeddable value object holding the ordered list of legs a cargo is routed along, and checking whether a handling event is expected by the itinerary.

nodes.name: Itinerary
nodes.summary: Value object with a list of Legs; exposes initial/final locations, final arrival date, and isExpected(HandlingEvent) logic with value-based equality.

nodes.name: isExpected
nodes.summary: Determines whether a handling event (receive, load, unload, claim) matches what the itinerary expects.

nodes.name: Leg.java
nodes.summary: Embeddable value object representing one voyage segment of an itinerary with load/unload locations and times.

nodes.name: Leg
nodes.summary: Immutable-style leg holding voyage, load and unload locations and times, with value-based equality.

nodes.name: RouteSpecification.java
nodes.summary: Value object specifying origin, destination and arrival deadline for a cargo, implemented as a specification that checks itineraries.

nodes.name: RouteSpecification
nodes.summary: Specification of a cargo's required route; isSatisfiedBy(Itinerary) verifies origin, destination and deadline.

nodes.name: Location.java
nodes.summary: JPA entity for a physical place (port, terminal) identified by UN/LOCODE, with an UNKNOWN sentinel.

nodes.name: Location
nodes.summary: Entity identified by UnLocode and name; identity-based equality via sameIdentityAs.

nodes.name: AbstractSpecification.java
nodes.summary: Base class for the Specification pattern providing and/or/not composition.

nodes.name: AbstractSpecification
nodes.summary: Abstract generic specification with isSatisfiedBy and composable and/or/not combinators.

nodes.name: MANIFEST.txt
nodes.summary: Plain-text manifest listing the domain module's Java source files with their dependency depth.

nodes.name: AndSpecification.java
nodes.summary: Composite specification that is satisfied only when both wrapped specifications are satisfied.

nodes.name: AndSpecification
nodes.summary: Composite specification that is satisfied only when both wrapped specifications are satisfied.

nodes.name: isSatisfiedBy
nodes.summary: Evaluates the candidate against the wrapped specification(s) and combines results with AND logic.

nodes.name: OrSpecification.java
nodes.summary: Composite specification that is satisfied when either wrapped specification is satisfied.

nodes.name: OrSpecification
nodes.summary: Composite specification that is satisfied when either wrapped specification is satisfied.

nodes.name: isSatisfiedBy
nodes.summary: Evaluates the candidate against the wrapped specification(s) and combines results with OR logic.

nodes.name: NotSpecification.java
nodes.summary: Decorator specification that negates the result of a wrapped specification.

nodes.name: NotSpecification
nodes.summary: Decorator specification that negates the result of a wrapped specification.

nodes.name: isSatisfiedBy
nodes.summary: Evaluates the candidate against the wrapped specification(s) and combines results with NOT logic.

nodes.name: Specification.java
nodes.summary: Generic Specification interface of the domain-driven design specification pattern, with isSatisfiedBy and and/or/not combinators.

nodes.name: Specification
nodes.summary: Interface declaring isSatisfiedBy plus and/or/not composition operations for business rules.

tour.title: Project Manifest
tour.description: Start with MANIFEST.txt, which lists the domain module's Java sources and their dependencies. This is a pure domain layer of Eclipse Cargo Tracker, built with DDD and Jakarta EE/JPA.

tour.title: Cargo: The Aggregate Root
tour.description: Cargo is the aggregate root: a shipment with a tracking id, route specification, itinerary and delivery snapshot. Everything else orbits it, and it exposes rerouting operations such as specifyNewRoute and assignToRoute.
tour.languageLesson: Java annotations like @Entity and @Embeddable mark JPA persistence roles. Entities have identity; embeddables are value objects stored inside the owner's table.

tour.title: Identity: TrackingId
tour.description: TrackingId is a small embeddable value object wrapping the unique cargo identifier. Equality is based on its value, not object identity.

tour.title: Routing Requirements and Plan
tour.description: RouteSpecification says where a cargo must go (origin, destination, deadline). Itinerary is the planned ordered list of Legs. Together they let the domain judge whether a plan satisfies the requirement and whether handling was expected.

tour.title: Locations in the Network
tour.description: Location is the most widely referenced entity (identified by UN/LOCODE). Routes, legs and events all point to it.

tour.title: Handling Events and History
tour.description: HandlingEvent records real-world activity (load, unload, receive, claim, customs). HandlingHistory orders these events and exposes the latest completed one.

tour.title: Delivery: Deriving Status
tour.description: Delivery is an immutable snapshot derived from route specification, itinerary and handling history. It computes transport status, routing status, misdirection and next expected activity, and Cargo refreshes it via deriveDeliveryProgress.

tour.title: The Specification Pattern
tour.description: Specification<T> declares isSatisfiedBy plus and/or/not composition. AbstractSpecification implements the combinators, while And, Or and Not specifications compose business rules. RouteSpecification builds on this.
tour.languageLesson: Generics (Specification<T>) let one rule interface work for any candidate type, and abstract classes share default combinator logic across subclasses.

tour.title: Shared Utilities
tour.description: DomainObjectUtils offers null-safe helpers used across the model, finishing the tour of the shared kernel.
